question: What score shows a normal, healthy deep tendon reflex?
explanation: A score of 2+ is the standard, expected normal response for deep tendon reflexes in healthy adults. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h7)

question: How do long-term conditions like diabetes mellitus usually affect our special senses over time?

options.A: They cause sudden and permanent total hearing loss within days.
options.B: They immediately destroy taste buds on the surface of the tongue.
options.C: They prevent the brain from processing any sensory information.
options.D: They slowly damage delicate blood vessels supplying sensory organs.

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar in diabetes slowly damages tiny blood vessels (microvascular damage). This is why chronic conditions often lead to gradual vision changes like retinopathy. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is required when a nurse needs to discard a leftover portion of liquid morphine?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist must inspect the empty syringe
options.B: Another nurse must witness and co-sign the disposal
options.C: The patient must sign a form confirming the waste
options.D: The nurse can throw it away alone at the end of the shift

explanation: A second witness prevents falsification and ensures leftover drugs are not diverted for illegal use. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h6)

question: The inner ear does more than just help us hear. What else is it responsible for?

options.A: It produces mucus to filter out dust and germs
options.B: It connects directly to the tonsils to fight throat infections
options.C: It amplifies sound waves before they reach the eardrum
options.D: It contains the vestibular system which controls body balance

explanation: Spot on! Aside from the cochlea helping with sound, your inner ear houses the vestibular system, which is basically your body's built-in balance and orientation center. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h1)

question: What key advice should a nurse give a patient starting daily levothyroxine?

options.A: Swallow the tablet with an antacid to protect your stomach lining.
options.B: Avoid taking the pill if your heart rate is above 90 beats per minute.
options.C: Take the dose right after a large evening meal to prevent nausea.
options.D: Take the medication on an empty stomach in the morning.

explanation: Well done! Food, iron, and calcium can trap levothyroxine in the gut, so taking it first thing on an empty stomach ensures the body absorbs it properly. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h5)

question: As a ward nurse handling hospital tools every day, what is your main responsibility regarding them?

options.A: Acting as primary custodian and daily operator
options.B: Purchasing replacement parts from suppliers
options.C: Designing and manufacturing new medical devices
options.D: Repairing all electrical faults on the ward

explanation: You use these tools right at the bedside every day, which means you are the key person making sure they are handled and checked properly! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.C: Maternal education and literacy rates
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for discharge on home IV antibiotics says they want to stop the medicine early because the pain is gone. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Suggest waiting until the next scheduled clinic visit in three months
options.B: Tell the patient to double their pill dose to make up for the missed days
options.C: Explain that stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and harder to treat
options.D: Agree and instruct the patient to take over-the-counter pain pills instead

explanation: Patients must finish their entire course of antibiotics to ensure all bacteria are eradicated, preventing a relapse of chronic osteomyelitis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h9)

question: How is disinfection different from sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization takes less time than standard chemical disinfection
options.B: Disinfection is only performed on human skin and living tissues
options.C: Disinfection does not destroy all bacterial spores like sterilization does
options.D: Sterilization uses chemical agents while disinfection only uses heat

explanation: Spot on! Sterilization is the heavy-duty process that wipes out every single trace of life, including tough spores. Disinfection cleans up most germs, but leaves spores behind. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit completely unresponsive after a road accident. Where should you get their health history?

options.A: Family members, emergency personnel, and previous medical records
options.B: Waiting until the patient wakes up before gathering any information
options.C: Guessing the past medical history based on the patient's age
options.D: Asking the patient's coworkers who are standing outside the room

explanation: Great job! When a patient can't speak for themselves, family members and past medical files are lifesavers for gathering background info. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why should hospital waste bags be tied up when they are only three-quarters full?

options.A: To ensure the waste weighs exactly the same as household garbage
options.B: To prevent overfilling, tearing, and accidental spills during transit
options.C: To give the cleaning staff enough time to take a lunch break
options.D: To allow the municipal collection agency to charge lower fees

explanation: Exactly! Leaving a bit of space at the top lets you tie the bag securely and stops nasty spills on the way out. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h6)

question: What causes the shoulder pain some patients feel after a laparoscopic surgery?

options.A: Strain from lifting heavy objects in the recovery room
options.B: Tight bandages applied around the upper chest area
options.C: An awkward position maintained during prolonged walking
options.D: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm

explanation: Spot on! Leftover gas can press against the diaphragm muscle, tricking the nerves into feeling like the pain is coming from the shoulder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: During a vaginal exam, you suddenly spot an umbilical cord prolapse. What is your very first emergency action?

options.A: Manually lift the presenting part off the cord to relieve pressure
options.B: Send the patient home to rest until the next scheduled clinic visit
options.C: Administer oral pain medication and document the finding later
options.D: Wait quietly for the next contraction to see if the cord recedes

explanation: Every second counts here! By using your hand to lift the baby's head off the cord, you keep oxygen flowing to the baby until delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h6)

question: Why is a fever in a neutropenic patient treated so aggressively?

options.A: It means the cancer has spread to the skin
options.B: They lack enough white blood cells to fight off hidden infections, leading to rapid sepsis
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs stop working completely if a fever develops
options.D: Fever automatically causes permanent brain damage within minutes

explanation: Without neutrophils, a minor infection can quickly overwhelm the body and cause fatal septic shock, requiring instant antibiotic therapy. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h4)

question: A nursing mother complains of sharp nipple pain and visible cracks. What should you as a nurse check first?

options.A: Suggest weaning the baby to formula immediately
options.B: Recommend applying strong antiseptic ointments before every feed
options.C: Assess the infant's latch technique and mouth positioning during feeding
options.D: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding completely for one week

explanation: Fixing how the baby takes the breast stops further damage and lets the skin heal naturally. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h3)

question: What do we call the infected clumps of platelets and germs that grow on heart valves in endocarditis?

options.A: Atheromas
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Thromboemboli

explanation: In infective endocarditis, clusters of bacteria, platelets, and fibrin build up on the valves like little growths called vegetations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is poor nutrition (malnutrition) such a big problem during cancer treatment?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent hair loss
options.B: It increases the likelihood of bone fractures
options.C: It prevents medications from dissolving in the stomach
options.D: It impairs wound healing and reduces treatment tolerance

explanation: Good food is body fuel! Without proper nutrition, the body struggles to heal wounds and handle harsh cancer treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the main advantage of an interprofessional healthcare team for an elderly patient?

options.A: Lower overall healthcare costs for the government
options.B: Comprehensive care that improves overall quality of life
options.C: Faster discharge from acute care hospitals
options.D: Elimination of the need for informal family caregivers

explanation: When different health professionals combine their skills, all aspects of the patient's physical, emotional, and social needs get covered, leading to happier, healthier days. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which young patient is most likely to need an oxygen tent?

options.A: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in an adult
options.B: Severe diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Decompensated heart failure with fluid overload
options.D: Acute bronchiolitis in a toddler

explanation: Spot on! Respiratory infections like bronchiolitis make it hard for little ones to breathe, making an oxygen tent a great choice to help them recover. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T10#GNS212_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why is keeping a look-out for fire hazards trickier in a patient's house compared to a hospital ward?

options.A: Private homes are always built using highly flammable wood
options.B: Hospitals have stricter rules against using electricity
options.C: Nurses have no legal authority to check home environments
options.D: Private homes have unpredictable layouts and lack institutional safety systems

explanation: Hospitals have built-in alarms, sprinklers, and standard designs. Every patient's home is different and usually lacks these heavy-duty safety backups. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T8#GNS324_U6_T8_h1)

question: Which federal law requires healthcare facilities to inform patients about advance directives upon admission?

options.A: The Patient Self-Determination Act
options.B: The Nursing Practice Act
options.C: The Health Insurance Portability Act
options.D: The Affordable Care Act

explanation: Passed in 1991, the Patient Self-Determination Act ensures that patients are told about their right to make advance directives when entering a healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the biggest benefit of practicing complex procedures on high-tech manikins in the simulation lab?

options.A: It removes the need for faculty members to observe student performance.
options.B: It completely replaces the need for written examinations in nursing school.
options.C: It guarantees that students will never make a mistake in the actual hospital.
options.D: Students can practice high-risk procedures without risking patient safety.

explanation: Simulation gives you a safe space to build confidence and master your hands-on skills before you ever touch a real patient. Brilliant learning environment! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h4)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in any hospital?

options.A: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Changing bed linen every morning
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves for all tasks

explanation: Spot on! Good old-fashioned hand hygiene is your number one weapon against hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why do nurses look at reproductive health as a lifelong journey rather than just a passing phase?

options.A: Because reproductive needs change and persist from birth to old age
options.B: Because healthcare funding is tied to lifelong patient monitoring
options.C: Because reproductive organs never undergo natural degeneration
options.D: Because patients only seek care during their childbearing years

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive health matters at every single stage of life, meaning our care and guidance as nurses never truly stop. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: How does a community health nurse's role differ from a hospital nurse?

options.A: The community nurse has no responsibility for patient health outcomes
options.B: The community nurse spends all shift managing mechanical ventilators
options.C: The community nurse strictly follows rigid hospital visiting rules
options.D: The community nurse focuses more on education, advocacy, and resource linkage

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses shine by teaching populations and connecting families to health resources around them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to ask about past surgical complications, such as a bad reaction to anesthesia?

options.A: To calculate the exact hospital bill in advance
options.B: To check if the patient has valid health insurance
options.C: To prevent similar dangerous reactions during future procedures
options.D: To determine what food the patient likes to eat

explanation: Knowing about previous adverse anesthesia reactions allows the surgical and anesthesia team to take safety precautions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why do doctors often use laparoscopy to look closely at the fallopian tubes?

options.A: It requires no anesthesia and is done at the bedside
options.B: It completely cures all tubal blockages
options.C: It uses high-frequency sound waves to measure organ density
options.D: It lets the surgeon see the pelvic organs directly with a camera

explanation: A laparoscope is a tiny lighted camera that gives the surgeon a clear, direct view of what is going on inside the pelvis. You're mastering this topic! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h4)

question: What is the best needle size for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 25 to 27 gauge, 1/4 to 1/2 inch long
options.B: 21 to 23 gauge, 1 inch long
options.C: 30 to 32 gauge, 2 inches long
options.D: 18 to 20 gauge, 1 to 1.5 inches long

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! A fine, short needle ensures the medicine stays shallow in the dermis rather than slipping into the fat below. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T8#GNS125_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why are infants gently placed in a restraining board or wrap during a circumcision?

options.A: To keep their body temperature elevated during the operation
options.B: To make it easier for the surgeon to place a urinary catheter
options.C: To prevent sudden movements that could lead to accidental injury
options.D: To stop them from crying out loudly during the procedure

explanation: Babies can't sit still on command! Soft restraints keep them safe and steady so the doctor can work safely with sharp instruments. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why must you check a baseline PTT before starting a patient on a heparin infusion?

options.A: To determine if the patient requires an emergency platelet transfusion
options.B: To calculate future dose adjustments safely against the patient's starting point
options.C: To prove the patient has never been exposed to anticoagulant medication
options.D: To check the patient's kidney function before drug administration begins

explanation: Everyone's blood clots a little differently. Knowing the patient's starting PTT helps you adjust their heparin drip safely without causing bleeding complications. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why should nurses use a friendly, non-judgmental tone when asking patients about drug use?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from malpractice suits
options.B: It encourages patients to provide honest health disclosures
options.C: It ensures the doctor prescribes higher drug doses
options.D: It prevents the patient from staying in the hospital

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from moral blame, they are much more honest about their health history. Great nursing care starts with empathy! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is assuming a community's health needs based only on past experience a major mistake?

options.A: Every community has unique conditions, and unverified assumptions lead to wasted resources
options.B: Illnesses never repeat themselves in the same geographic location twice
options.C: Community members prefer foreign nurses to local healthcare workers
options.D: Past experience is legally forbidden in public health practice

explanation: Relying on assumptions instead of current local data often results in interventions that do not match real community needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the main job of mineralocorticoids in the human body?

options.A: Regulating sodium and fluid balance
options.B: Suppressing white blood cell activity
options.C: Increasing protein synthesis in muscles
options.D: Lowering high blood sugar levels

explanation: Mineralocorticoids (like aldosterone) work on the kidneys to manage salt (sodium) and water in your body. It's all about keeping your fluid balance steady! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h2)

question: What usually happens to the rate at which the kidneys filter blood (GFR) during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It increases by about fifty percent.
options.B: It drops sharply during the third trimester.
options.C: It remains completely unchanged.
options.D: It decreases by about fifty percent.

explanation: Your kidneys work overtime during pregnancy, filtering blood at a much higher rate to handle waste for both mum and baby. Amazing how the body adapts! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: Why is misoprostol taken after mifepristone instead of taking it first?

options.A: It softens the cervix before the mifepristone is absorbed.
options.B: It triggers contractions to expel tissue loosened by the first drug.
options.C: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.
options.D: It neutralizes the extreme toxicity of the first drug.

explanation: Great thinking! Mifepristone loosens the pregnancy tissue first, so when misoprostol comes in to cause uterine contractions, it can easily push the tissue out. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: Which two major bone fractures are notorious for causing massive internal bleeding?

options.A: Pelvis and femur
options.B: Phalanges and carpals
options.C: Clavicle and scapula
options.D: Radius and ulna

explanation: Large bones like the pelvis and femur are packed with blood vessels and bone marrow. When they break, they can bleed significantly inside the body before anyone even notices. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h2)

question: What is the big win of using laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: General anesthesia is never required during laparoscopic pelvic procedures
options.B: It provides a clear view of internal organs without needing any camera lights
options.C: Smaller incisions lead to faster physical recovery and less postoperative pain
options.D: Patients can leave the hospital immediately before the procedure even finishes

explanation: Correct! Tiny puncture holes mean less body trauma, quicker healing, and way less pain for the patient. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is palliative care ideally introduced before the very final days of a degenerative illness?

options.A: To allow a smooth transition and build relationships with the care team
options.B: To guarantee that the patient will regain full physical mobility
options.C: To speed up the natural progression of the genetic disorder
options.D: To eliminate the need for any medications or nursing oversight

explanation: Early introduction helps patients and families process difficult decisions and builds trust with the palliative team before a crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h8)

question: If you notice widespread tiny red spots (petechiae) on a patient's skin, what does that usually suggest?

options.A: An excess of circulating vitamin K
options.B: Chronic inflammation of the large joints
options.C: An abnormality or low count of platelets
options.D: A complete absence of clotting factor VIII

explanation: Petechiae happen when tiny tiny blood vessels (capillaries) leak because there aren't enough healthy platelets around to keep them sealed. Good clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h5)

question: When should a PAC clinic refer a patient to a higher-level surgical facility?

options.A: Whenever the client requests oral contraceptive pills for birth control
options.B: When the patient presents with signs of uterine perforation or severe bowel injury
options.C: As a routine step for every single woman who seeks post-abortion care
options.D: Only after the client has stayed in the clinic for two weeks

explanation: Complex emergencies like organ perforation go beyond basic primary clinics and need specialist surgical care to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: What is the correct order of the three stages in Hans Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Alarm, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Alarm, resistance, exhaustion
options.C: Exhaustion, resistance, alarm
options.D: Resistance, alarm, exhaustion

explanation: Think of it as a journey: your body first sounds the alarm when stressed, tries to fight back during resistance, and finally gets worn out in exhaustion if the stress doesn't stop. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h1)

question: What visual characteristic does urine often have in a patient with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: Dark red and bloody
options.B: Frothy or foamy appearance
options.C: Thick and milky white
options.D: Bright neon green color

explanation: The large amount of protein spilling into the urine changes its surface tension, creating a noticeable frothy or foamy look when the patient voids. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: What do we call a drug's special superpower of harming bacteria without damaging human cells?

options.A: Broad spectrum
options.B: Bacteriostatic action
options.C: Selective toxicity
options.D: Acquired resistance

explanation: You got it! Selective toxicity means the drug safely attacks unique parts of the bacteria while sparing our own human cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h2)

question: Why are unsafe injection practices such a big public health problem?

options.A: They make injectable medications completely ineffective
options.B: They increase the physical pain of receiving treatment
options.C: They rapidly spread blood-borne pathogens to large numbers of people
options.D: They cause immediate allergic reactions in all recipients

explanation: Sharing needles or contaminating medication vials can quickly transmit serious blood-borne infections across many patients in a short time. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of physiotherapy in long-term MS care?

options.A: Maintaining mobility and preventing joint stiffness
options.B: Analyzing cerebrospinal fluid laboratory samples
options.C: Performing surgical repair of demyelinated nerves
options.D: Prescribing disease-modifying drug dosages

explanation: Physiotherapy keeps muscles working, improves balance, and prevents tight joints (contractures), helping the patient stay active for as long as possible. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of cancer screening programs in primary health care?

options.A: To find out the patient's family tree
options.B: To completely replace laboratory blood tests
options.C: To perform major cancer surgeries
options.D: To catch abnormalities before symptoms and spreading happen

explanation: Screening is all about catching issues early when treatment is easiest and most successful. Prevention is better than cure! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h5)

question: What main event causes urine to leak out in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Complete blockage of the urethra
options.B: An overactive detrusor muscle spasm
options.C: A sudden urinary tract infection
options.D: Sudden physical pressure on the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Stress incontinence happens when sudden physical pressure—like coughing, laughing, or lifting—pushes urine out because the bladder pressure beats the urethra's grip. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: A patient recovering from a long, difficult labor reports a constant, uncontrolled leak of urine from her vagina. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Vaginal fistula
options.B: Simple rectocele
options.C: Transverse septum
options.D: Imperforate hymen

explanation: That's correct! Prolonged pressure during a tough labor can damage the tissue wall between the bladder and vagina, creating an abnormal opening (a fistula) that leaks urine. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h3)

question: Why must you let the skin antiseptic dry completely before inserting the needle?

options.A: Antiseptic works only when it turns into a white powder
options.B: Wet alcohol destroys the sharpness of the needle tip
options.C: Dry skin is tougher and holds the needle steadier
options.D: Wet alcohol causes a stinging sensation when pierced

explanation: That's right! Letting the alcohol dry lets it kill germs properly and stops wet alcohol from entering the puncture wound, which would sting terribly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the term for high blood pressure that has no single identifiable medical cause?

options.A: Primary hypertension
options.B: Malignant hypertension
options.C: Gestational hypertension
options.D: Secondary hypertension

explanation: Primary or essential hypertension makes up the vast majority of cases and develops gradually from lifestyle and genetic factors. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h2)

question: Why do patients with viral hepatitis turn yellow (jaundice)?

options.A: Excessive production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: Severe dehydration concentrating bile pigments in the skin
options.C: Damaged liver cells cannot process and clear out bilirubin
options.D: Direct bacterial infection of the superficial skin layers

explanation: When liver cells are inflamed, they struggle to process bilirubin properly. This yellow pigment builds up in the blood and skin, causing jaundice. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h2)

question: What usually happens if a patient's thinking part of the brain is badly damaged, but their brainstem is totally fine?

options.A: The patient loses awareness of the environment but may still sleep and wake
options.B: The patient loses all reflex actions while keeping clear thoughts
options.C: The patient stays completely awake but loses the ability to feel pain
options.D: The patient enters an immediate state of permanent brain death

explanation: You're doing great! Because the brainstem handles sleep-wake cycles, an undamaged brainstem means the body can still cycle between sleeping and waking up, even without higher thinking. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which Nigerian agency is in charge of enforcing environmental and waste laws?

options.A: Nigerian Football Federation
options.B: NESREA
options.C: National Youth Service Corps
options.D: Federal Road Safety Corps

explanation: Spot on! NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) sets and enforces laws to protect Nigeria's environment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which nursing action helps a hospitalized patient cough up thick mucus more easily?

options.A: Encouraging fluids and deep breathing exercises
options.B: Keeping the patient lying flat in bed all day
options.C: Restricting water to prevent fluid buildup in the lungs
options.D: Giving strong sleeping pills to stop the cough

explanation: Water is a natural thinner for mucus! Combined with deep breathing and controlled coughing, it helps clear the airways safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h7)

question: A stroke patient can walk with a walker, but struggles to button their shirt. Which team member should help with this?

options.A: The occupational therapist
options.B: The physical therapist
options.C: The speech-language pathologist
options.D: The vocational case manager

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) love working on everyday tasks! They specialize in fine motor skills like dressing, grooming, and feeding. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h4)

question: After a punch biopsy on the arm, a little blood keeps oozing out. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Flush the open wound with sterile hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Remove the newly placed sutures to inspect the base
options.C: Apply direct firm pressure with sterile gauze
options.D: Immediately apply a full-thickness skin graft

explanation: Simple, direct pressure with sterile gauze is your best friend for stopping minor bleeding before doing anything else. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is a very common underlying cause of autonomic neuropathy in clinical practice?

options.A: Severe bone fractures
options.B: Acute muscle strain
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic iron deficiency

explanation: Over time, persistently high blood sugar levels damage peripheral nerves. This makes diabetic autonomic neuropathy a frequent finding you will encounter in clinical wards. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main job of a midwifery kit in community health work?

options.A: To provide tools and meds for childbirth care and quick emergency help
options.B: To serve as a mini operating room for a big city hospital
options.C: To store personal items for community health workers during long trips
options.D: To collect lab samples for community malaria screening

explanation: Think of the midwifery kit as a birth attendant's best friend in the field—it packs all the essential tools and meds needed to safely manage deliveries at the primary healthcare level! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h1)

question: What do we call a pregnancy where a mother is carrying two or more babies at the same time?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy

question: What is the purpose of recommending pelvic floor exercises in the long-term recovery phase?

options.D: To provide stability and protect the limb during movement.

explanation: Supporting the limbs properly keeps the movement steady and shields the surrounding tissues from unnecessary strain. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which antibodies are naturally present in the plasma of a person with Type A blood?

options.A: Anti-B antibodies
options.B: Anti-A antibodies
options.C: No ABO antibodies at all
options.D: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies

explanation: Type A blood has A antigens on the cells, so the body develops anti-B antibodies to attack foreign B types. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h2)

question: What do we call a colostomy problem where the bowel telescopes out and the stoma becomes way too long?

options.A: Retraction
options.B: Hernia
options.C: Necrosis
options.D: Prolapse

explanation: Correct! A prolapse happens when extra bowel pushes out through the stoma site, making it stick out much further than normal. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h6)

question: What happens when fertilization does NOT take place during the cycle?

options.A: Progesterone drops and the uterine lining sheds
options.B: Progesterone rises and the uterine lining thickens further
options.C: Estrogen disappears completely and ovulation happens again
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin spikes in the blood

explanation: When pregnancy doesn't happen, the corpus luteum fades, progesterone levels fall, and the body sheds the uterine lining as a menstrual period. Totally normal physiology! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which blood test results confirm primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum hormone
options.C: High serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and high parathyroid hormone

explanation: In primary hyperparathyroidism, an overactive gland pumps out too much PTH, which in turn drives your blood calcium levels way up. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common mental health challenge for survivors of ongoing abuse?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Well done! Survivors often deal with lasting emotional impacts like anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h3)

question: Which international bodies often partner to support Nigeria's family planning supplies?

options.A: World Trade Organization
options.B: OPEC Petroleum Board
options.C: UNFPA and USAID
options.D: International Labour Organization

explanation: Organizations like UNFPA (United Nations Population Fund) and USAID play a massive role in funding and shipping family planning commodities to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical behavioral warning sign of an eating disorder in a teenager?

options.A: Obsessive preoccupation with calorie counting and food labels
options.B: Eating large balanced meals happily with family every evening
options.C: Wearing oversized clothing to hide noticeable weight loss
options.D: Frequent trips to the bathroom immediately following meals

explanation: Spot on! Teens with eating disorders usually avoid family dinners or hide their eating habits, rather than happily enjoying big meals with everyone. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is part of a psychosocial assessment?

options.A: Checking the range of motion in the patient's knee joint
options.B: Evaluating the patient's coping mechanisms and support systems
options.C: Listening for abnormal breath sounds in the lower lobes
options.D: Reviewing lab results for elevated white blood cells

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial checks look at mental health, how well the patient handles stress, and who is there to support them at home. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a chemical barrier part of our innate defense?

options.A: Cytotoxic T-cell activation
options.B: Keratin in the outer skin layer
options.C: Lysozyme in tears and saliva
options.D: Antibodies produced by plasma cells

explanation: You're right! Lysozyme is a natural germ-killer found in our tears and saliva that breaks open bacterial walls. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is 'Disturbed Body Image' a common nursing diagnosis for conditions like Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Visible physical changes like weight gain and facial swelling alter a person's appearance.
options.B: Hormonal imbalances cause permanent memory loss and confusion.
options.C: Severe muscle weakness prevents the patient from looking in a mirror.
options.D: Patients lose their sense of hearing and balance due to inner ear fluid shifts.

explanation: Spot on. Cushing's brings noticeable body changes, like round 'moon facies' and weight shifts, which can be really tough on a patient's self-esteem. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for surgery takes daily aspirin for joint pain. What is your main concern as their nurse?

options.A: Aspirin causes a dangerous spike in white blood cell counts
options.B: Aspirin inhibits platelet function and can cause excessive bleeding
options.C: Aspirin turns the patient's blood bright green in the tubing
options.D: Aspirin completely stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Aspirin stops platelets from sticking together properly. Before surgery, this puts the patient at high risk for heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h6)

question: You are about to check the oral temperature of a patient whose skin is intact. What should you do about gloves?

options.A: Skip gloves because skin is intact and no fluids are expected
options.B: Wear standard examination gloves just in case
options.C: Put on sterile surgical gloves
options.D: Wear heavy-duty utility gloves

explanation: For routine checks involving unbroken skin and no body fluids, gloves aren't needed. This saves precious hospital supplies and time! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What are the two main hormone types found in combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Prolactin and progestin
options.B: Progesterone and testosterone
options.C: Estrogen and oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen and progestin

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives contain a blend of synthetic estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h1)
